correctness.rationale: For all odd n>=5 the real circulant Fourier spectrum is exactly 2 sum_{r=1}^{(n-1)/2} r^p cos(2*pi*j*r/n). At p=1 every nonconstant mode has eigenvalue at most -1/4; fixed even modes tend to -1/4 and fixed odd modes to -infinity. The n^{-t/n^2} rescaling gives a uniform O(n^-2) Taylor remainder, and bounded variation of x log x yields a uniform O(1/j) normalized-derivative tail. The fixed even derivative integrals are exactly F(2*pi*k)/(8*pi^2*k^2) with a strict maximum at k=1. A finite-low-frequency/high-frequency split proves both sides of the sharp limit, with no extrapolation. Numerical checks of multiple n corroborate but do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The generalized-roundness exponent of the canonical odd-cycle Cayley metric is a natural Hilbert-snowflake invariant. The exact n^-2 decay coefficient and controlling Fourier mode quantify a gap that earlier qualitative convergence estimates could not resolve. Comparison against the independently characterized four-point roundness reveals a mathematically substantive n^-1 versus n^-2 distinction in the same metric family; neither is an arbitrary parameter slice.
